# Behavior DSL

Each part of a behavior definition: what it makes osapi do, and when to use it.
`osapi behavior spec get` prints the same list from this build.
[Building a behavior](../behaviors.md) tells how to write one.

## Definition

### `Register(Define(name, doc, options...))`

Declares the behavior and adds it to the registry. The agent, the server, the
CLI and the generator read the registry. The name is the route, the command, the
permission and the docs page: lowercase letters and digits, no dash. The Go
package is where the definition lives, which osapi behavior create --package
sets when the name is a Go keyword.

Use: One time, in behavior.go: var Behavior =
behavior.Register(behavior.Define(...)).

## Options of Define

### `Node`

Runs the methods on a host, through the job system.

Use: Always. It is the only placement.

### `API`

Serves the methods over REST, with routes, permissions and the OpenAPI spec.

Use: When an operator or a program calls the behavior.

### `CLI`

Makes osapi client commands and their docs pages. Needs API.

Use: When an operator calls the behavior from a shell.

### `Of(parent.Behavior)`

Puts the behavior's items under an item of another behavior: Of(user.Behavior)
puts sshkey at /api/node/&#123;hostname&#125;/user/&#123;name&#125;/sshkey and
osapi client node user sshkey. Each input has the parent's key, such as name,
which goes in the path before the method's own key. The permissions are the
parent's: the keys of a user need user:read and user:write. The parent's
provider is not required: a child that needs it declares Requires too.

Use: For a resource that exists only inside another, such as the SSH keys of a
user. Not with Under: the parent's path is the group.

### `Area(AreaName)`

Puts a served behavior in an area of the UI: the group of the Configure page's
Add Block panel that its blocks sit in. Use a constant: AreaServices,
AreaSoftware, AreaConfig, AreaNode, AreaNetworking, AreaSecurity, AreaCommand,
AreaHardware or AreaContainers.

Use: On each behavior with API. behavior validate refuses a served behavior with
none.

### `Under(GroupName)`

Nests the behavior in a group: its routes, commands, directory and the prefix of
its permissions. Use a constant, such as GroupNetwork; behavior validate refuses
a group outside KnownGroups, because a misspelled group makes a new route,
command and permission.

Use: When the behavior belongs to a group, such as network. Add the group's
constant to KnownGroups first.

### `Internal`

Gives the behavior no route, command or permission. Only the behaviors that
require it can call it.

Use: For work that two behaviors share, such as writing a file.

### `Requires(behaviors...)`

Builds the providers of those behaviors first. The builder gets them with
host.Require.

Use: When the behavior uses the methods of another behavior.

### `Platform(PlatformDebian, build)`

Builds the provider on that platform: a distribution, darwin, or linux for each
Linux host without its own. On another platform, the methods report skipped. Use
a constant: PlatformDebian, PlatformDarwin or PlatformLinux. behavior validate
refuses a name outside KnownPlatforms, here and in On, RunsOnPlatform and
OnPlatform.

Use: One time for each platform that the behavior supports.

### `Sudo(programs...)`

Lists the programs that the providers run with sudo. The agent preflight checks
that sudo allows each.

Use: For each program that needs root.

### `Runs(programs...)`

Lists the programs that the providers run without sudo. The agent warns when one
is not installed. Runs(behavior.AnyProgram), "\*", is each program: the agent
and the integration test look for none.

Use: For each program that does not need root. AnyProgram only for a behavior
that runs the program its caller names, such as command.

### `RunsOnPlatform(platform, programs...)`

Lists the programs that the providers run without sudo on one platform only.
linux is each platform that is not darwin. The agent and the integration test
ask for them on that platform only.

Use: For a program that only one platform has, such as vm_stat or sw_vers on
darwin.

### `SudoOnPlatform(platform, programs...)`

Lists the programs that the provider declared for one platform runs with sudo.
They hold on each host that this provider serves, so linux does not hold on
debian when the behavior declares a debian provider. The agent and the
integration test ask for them there only.

Use: For a program that each platform's provider runs in its own way, such as
update-ca-certificates on debian and update-ca-trust on linux.

### `RunsIfPresent(programs...)`

Lists the programs that the providers run only when the host has them. The fake
host permits them, and the agent and the integration test do not ask for them.

Use: For a program that a provider reads without, when it is missing, such as
zfs.

### `Writes("/etc/x.d/osapi-*.conf")`

Lists the paths that the providers write, remove or change the mode of. Each
such call is a file span in a trace. "\*" is the path that the caller names.

Use: For each path, also when a required behavior, such as managedfile, does the
write.

### `KeepsState`

Says that the providers keep a record in the file-state bucket. Each read and
write of it is a kv span.

Use: When the behavior keeps a record of what it wrote.

### `Config(defaults)`

Declares settings under behaviors.&lt;name&gt;, with a flag and an environment
variable for each. A provider reads them with Settings.

Use: For standing config of the agent. A value for one call is an input.

### `Validator("tag", check, schema, message)`

Declares a validate tag of the behavior, with the check that the server runs and
its schema in the spec, such as rule.Pattern(re).

Use: When no standard validate tag checks a value.

## Methods

### `Read("name", fn)`

A method that reads the host: GET and &lt;group&gt;:read. Named list, get or
status.

Use: For each read. fn is func(ctx, p Provider, in In) (Out, error).

### `Write("name", fn)`

A method that changes the host: POST, PUT or DELETE, and &lt;group&gt;:write.
Named create, update or delete. Out has Changed bool.

Use: For each change. fn is func(ctx, p Provider, in In) (Out, error).

### `Action("name", fn)`

A write named for what it does, such as restart: POST on the method's path with
the name after it, /service/&#123;name&#125;/restart, and &lt;group&gt;:execute,
which the operator role gets and automation does not. Named with one of the
CLI's actions. Out has Changed bool.

Use: For a change that create, update and delete do not say, such as start,
stop, restart, enable, signal or reboot.

## Refinements of a method

### `.Key("field")`

Puts that input field in the route and the CLI, and records it on the span of
each call. The field is validate:"required": a path segment is never empty.

Use: On each method that acts on one item, such as get, update and delete of a
key.

### `.NotAFact("why")`

Says why a read runs a command outside gohai: what it reads is not a fact of the
host, such as the updates of the package index. Without it, the tests of a read
fail on each command that does not go through gohai.

Use: Only when no gohai collector can have the value, because the host does not
own it. A fact that gohai does not read is a change to gohai first.

### `.PermitAs(verb) on an action`

Makes the action's permission &lt;name&gt;:&lt;verb&gt; in place of
&lt;name&gt;:execute, such as container:exec with behavior.VerbExec. Thus the
action does not share a permission with the other actions of its behavior, which
the operator role gets. Only the admin role gets the verb: behavior.VerbExec or
behavior.VerbShell. behavior validate refuses it on a method that is not an
action, and a different verb.

Use: For an action that runs a command that the caller gives, such as docker
exec, when the other actions of its behavior are for the operator role, such as
docker start.

### `.Shell() on an action`

Is .PermitAs(behavior.VerbShell): the action's permission is &lt;name&gt;:shell.
Only the admin role gets a shell permission. behavior validate refuses it on a
method that is not an action.

Use: For an action that runs a shell command line, such as command shell.

### `.Always()`

Marks an action that changes the host each time it runs, such as restart. Its
output reports changed: true on each run, and the generated test does not run it
again to see changed: false. behavior validate refuses it on a method that is
not an action.

Use: On an action that has no state to compare, so a second run is not
unchanged.

### `.Disrupts("why")`

Marks a method that takes the host down, such as a reboot or a shutdown, and
says why. Its examples run on the fake host, but the integration test never runs
them on a live host. behavior validate refuses it with no reason.

Use: On a method whose run would take down the host that the test runs on.

### `.Describe("text")`

The one-line description of the method, in the help, the spec and the docs.

Use: On each method.

### `.On(platform...)`

Limits the method to some of the platforms the behavior declares, such as
behavior.PlatformDebian. Elsewhere it reports skipped, and its examples run only
with the providers that serve it.

Use: When one method cannot run where the others do: a hostname read works on
macOS, but its update runs only on debian.

### `` `.Sudo(program...)` and `.Runs(program...)` on a method ``

Programs only this method runs, with sudo or without. A host needs them only
where the method runs, so the agent's startup check and the integration test ask
for them there only.

Use: With On, for a program the other platforms do not have, such as hostnamectl
for a hostname update.

### `.Before(fn) on a method`

Runs fn, func(ctx context.Context, in In) (In, error), on the controller in the
method's route, in a span of its own, before osapi queues the job. It changes
what the caller sent into what the agent gets, such as a password into its hash
with password.Hash. Each field tagged secret:"true" must be empty after it: else
the job is not queued, so the plain secret never goes in the job data, NATS or
the job KV.

Use: When the agent must not see a secret in plain text. Tag the field that the
step fills before:"set", and clear the secret in the step.

### `.AdminOnly() on a method`

Makes the permission of the method's verb, such as &lt;name&gt;:write, one that
only the admin role grants. With no mark, admin gets each permission; operator
each read and each execute permission, and automation each read and each write
permission, that is not admin only; read each read that is not admin only;
auditor and observer get their lists. An action's permission is
&lt;name&gt;:execute. Each method with the same verb must agree. osapi token
roles get --name automation shows what a role gets.

Use: For a write that is a trust decision or reaches root, which automation must
not make, such as an account or a cron entry.

### `.Explain("text")`

The longer description: what the method touches, and what a second call does.

Use: When one line does not say what the method changes.

### `.Example("doc", in, out, host...)`

A sample call. The docs page shows it, and the provider tests run it on a fake
host.

Use: On each method. A CLI behavior needs one.

### `.Fails("doc", in, "error text", host...)`

A call that the method refuses. The docs page lists it, the provider tests check
the error, and an input that breaks a validate rule is a generated HTTP test
that answers 400. Each rule of an input field has a .Fails input that breaks it,
which the API refuses with 400. An endpoint's required needs one, with the field
empty; a behavior's needs none, as its generated tests leave the field out. A
path field's required, and a min of 1 on a string that is required, optional or
in the path, need none: their only bad value is empty.

Use: For each rule of each input field, as validate requires, and for each input
that the method refuses for another reason.

## Hosts and effects of an example

### `After(input)`

Runs the method of that input before the example.

Use: When the example needs state, such as a parameter that is already managed.

### `Prints("command", "output")`

Says what a command prints on the fake host.

Use: For each command that the provider reads.

### `PrintsAfter("after", "command", "output")`

Says what a command prints after another command has run.

Use: For state that a program keeps, not a file.

### `Exits("command", 1)`

Says the exit code of a command on the fake host, as RunCmdFull returns it. A
command with no Exits exits 0.

Use: For a method that answers with the exit code of the command it runs, such
as command exec.

### `Stored(name, content, contentType)`

Says the object store of the fleet has the object name, with its content and its
content type, client.ContentRaw or client.ContentTemplate, as osapi client file
upload stores it. A provider reads it with h.Objects.Object.

Use: For an example of a behavior that deploys an uploaded file, such as through
the object building block.

### `Exists("path", "content")`

Puts a file on the fake host before the call.

Use: When the call reads or changes a file that is there.

### `ExistsAfter("after", "path", "content")`

Says what a file holds on the fake host after a command has run.

Use: For a file that a program changes, such as /etc/group after groupadd.
Declare its content before with Exists.

### `NotLive("why")`

Keeps a write example off the live host of the integration test, which skips it
and says why. The provider tests still run it on the fake host.

Use: Only for a write whose starting state the behavior's own methods cannot
make on a real host, such as the process that a signal stops. Test it in the lab
by hand, and say how in the definition.

### `Links("path", "target")`

Puts a symbolic link to target on the fake host before the call.

Use: When the call reads a link, such as /etc/localtime for the timezone.

### `Wrote("path", "content")`

Says that the call leaves the file with that content.

Use: For each file that the call writes.

### `Removed("path")`

Says that the call removes the file.

Use: For each file that the call removes.

### `Ran("program", args...)`

Says that the call runs the command.

Use: For each command that the call runs to make a change.

### `A write example on a live host`

CI runs each write example as root on a throwaway Linux runner, with
OSAPI_INTEGRATION_WRITE_BEHAVIORS=1, and the lab can run it too. Each example
starts with its item deleted, runs the calls of After, then must report its
changed, and changed: false when it runs again. The test uploads each object of
Stored first, and runs an .Always() action once. Prints, PrintsAfter and Exists
only answer the fake host.

Use: For each write example: give the state that it starts from with After,
which a real host can run, such as After(StartInput&#123;...&#125;) before a
stop, and make the content real, such as a unit file whose ExecStart exists. Run
it against the lab with go test -tags integration before you push.

## The host a provider gets

### `h.Platform, h.Container, h.Hostname`

The platform of the agent as gohai names it, such as debian or darwin; whether
the agent runs in a container; and its hostname. The tests build the provider
once for each platform that the behavior declares, with behaviortest.Hostname.

Use: To choose what a builder returns. A builder that cannot manage the host,
such as a writer in a container, returns the reader, or ErrUnsupported so the
methods report skipped.

### `h.Facts`

The facts that the agent collected last, by their JSON names, as a func that
returns them. A template that the provider renders with behavior.Render reads
them as .Facts. The tests give none, so a template example reads only its vars.

Use: Only to render a template that a person uploaded. A value that the provider
uses itself comes from a gohai collector.

### `h.FS`

The filesystem of the host, an avfs.VFS. The agent gives the real one. The tests
give an in-memory one, so an example says the files before the call with Exists
and Links, and the files after it with Wrote and Removed.

Use: For each file that the provider reads or writes itself, never the os
package. A file that osapi owns goes through managedfile; atomicfile.Write
writes one in place.

### `h.Exec`

Runs a program: RunCmd as the agent's user, RunPrivilegedCmd with sudo,
RunPrivilegedCmdWithStdin for a secret, RunPrivilegedCmdFull for a command whose
standard output, standard error and exit code the caller gets, such as docker
exec, RunCmdFull for the same as the agent's user, in a directory and with a
timeout, such as command exec. The tests give a generated mock that records each
command line and prints what the example says with Prints and PrintsAfter; Ran
checks a command after. Each program is declared with Runs or Sudo.

Use: For a write, such as systemctl start or apt-get install, and for a read of
what is not a fact of the host, with .NotAFact. A read of a fact goes through
h.Sources().

### `h.CommandEnabled`

The agent's agent.command.enabled: false refuses each command that a caller
names. The tests give true.

Use: In a method that runs a command the caller names, such as docker exec:
refuse the call when it is false, as the command DSL does.

### `h.Sources()`

The sources that a gohai collector reads the host through: h.FS, h.Exec, h.Now
and h.Resolver. Thus services.NewWith(h.Sources()).Collect(ctx, nil) reads the
real host on an agent and the fake host in the tests, with the files of Exists
and the commands of Prints.

Use: For each read of a fact of the host. The gohai test check fails a read that
runs a command another way.

### `h.FileState, h.FileStateBucket`

The KV store where osapi keeps a record of each file that it wrote, and its
bucket. nil when the agent has no store. The tests give an in-memory store.

Use: Only through managedfile, which declares KeepsState. A provider does not
read or write records itself.

### `h.Objects`

Reads an object of the Object Store, such as a file that osapi client file
upload stored. nil when the agent has no store. The tests give the objects of
Stored.

Use: Only through the object building block, which the behavior requires.

### `h.Settings, h.Required`

The decoded settings of the behavior, which Settings\[T](h) reads, and the
providers of the behaviors that it requires, which Require reads. The tests give
the defaults of Config and the real providers of the required behaviors, on the
same fake host.

Use: Through Settings\[T](h) and Require\[P](h, b), not the fields.

### `h.Now, h.Time()`

The clock of the host. Time reads it. The tests give behaviortest.Now,
2026-01-02 03:04:05 UTC.

Use: For each time that a provider computes, such as an uptime from a boot time.
Never time.Now.

### `h.Resolver, h.Logger`

The name resolver that gohai uses, such as for the canonical FQDN, and the
logger of the agent. The tests give a resolver that answers without the network,
and a logger that discards.

Use: The resolver goes to gohai through h.Sources(). Log with h.Logger only what
a span does not carry.

## Calls in a provider

### `collector.NewWith(h.Sources())`

Reads the facts of the host through gohai, such as
services.NewWith(h.Sources()).Collect(ctx, nil). Sources gives gohai the host's
filesystem and commands, so the tests run it on the fake host.

Use: For each read of a fact of the host: its packages, services, interfaces,
routes, disks. A provider runs h.Exec for writes, and reads with it only what is
not a fact, with .NotAFact.

### `atomicfile.Write(ctx, h.FS, path, content, mode)`

Writes the file atomically, in a file.write span. atomicfile.Remove and
atomicfile.Chmod make file.remove and file.chmod spans.

Use: In a building block that writes files. A behavior that manages a file
requires managedfile instead. A change through h.FS fails the tests.

### `Render(text, TemplateData{Facts, Vars, Hostname})`

Renders a template with the facts of the agent, the vars of the request and the
hostname. A key that the data does not have is an error.

Use: In the provider of a method with a template input. The input is checked at
the API already.

### `Settings[T](Behavior)`

Returns the settings of the behavior, or the defaults.

Use: In a builder or a method that reads a setting.

### `rule.Register("tag", rule.Pattern(re))`

Declares what a custom validate rule means in the spec: rule.Pattern(re),
rule.Format(f), or rule.None for a rule that the spec cannot show, such as a
target the controller resolves.

Use: Beside the validator of a new custom rule, in internal/validation.

## Errors a provider returns

### `behavior.ErrNotFound`

The item that the request names is not on the host: a service, a package, a key,
or an object of a deploy. On one host the API answers 404, on any method; on a
broadcast the row of the host is failed with the message.

Use: Wrap it with what was missing: fmt.Errorf("service %q: %w", name,
behavior.ErrNotFound). An update, a delete or an action on an item that osapi
does not have is not found; a delete of it is changed: false instead.

### `behavior.ErrNotManaged`

The item is on the host, but osapi did not deploy it, so osapi does not change
it, such as a file with no record in managedfile. The API answers 409.

Use: Before a write over an item that something else owns. Ask managedfile, not
the path: the agent's own unit is osapi-agent.service.

### `behavior.ErrNotInstalled`

A program that the method needs is not on the host. The API answers 409.

Use: When a method needs a program that the platform does not always have, and
Runs or RunsIfPresent does not say it.

### `behavior.ErrUnsupported`

The method does not apply to this host: its platform, or a container. The row of
the host is skipped, not failed.

Use: From a builder, for a platform or a host that it cannot manage, or from a
method that does not apply. Use .On or a reader builder first, so the definition
says it.

## Building on other behaviors

### `Chains`

A behavior that requires others calls them on the same host, in the same job:
dns calls netplan, and netplan calls managedfile. osapi behavior chain spec get
has how to build one, its rules and the building blocks in this binary; osapi
behavior chain get shows what each call sends and gets.

Use: Before a provider does generic work itself, such as writing a file that
osapi manages.

## Tags on input, output and settings fields

### `json:"name"`

The name of the field in the request, the flag, the column and --json. A field
with no json name fails the input or output rule, because the CLI and the tables
cannot show it. An optional field of a write's body, validate:"omitempty,...",
is json:"name,omitempty" too, or the client sends "" for it (the optional rule).
No input field is named hostname or target: every request has those.

Use: On each field.

### `validate:"..."`

The rules the server checks before the method runs: a value that breaks one is a
400 with &#123;"error": "..."&#125;. required makes the field required, oneof
gives an enum, min, max and len the length of a string, the items of an array or
the bounds of a number, startswith a pattern, and uuid, email, hostname, ip,
ipv4, ipv6, cidr, url and uri a format. The spec carries these, and the whole
tag in x-oapi-codegen-extra-tags. A custom rule, such as sysctl_key, needs its
schema from rule.Register; a rule with none fails the spec. In a behavior, the
agent and behavior.Call check the same rules before each method runs, so an
internal behavior's rules hold too; the author writes no check.

Use: On each input field. A field with no limit is validate:"omitempty";
validate refuses an input field with no tag.

### `default:"..."`

Not on a behavior input: the spec and the flag would show the default, but the
server does not apply it, so a caller of the API gets the zero value. The input
rule fails it.

Use: Never on a behavior input. The provider treats the empty value as the
default, and the doc says what it is.

### `doc:"..."`

The description in the spec, the flag help and the docs pages. The input rule
fails an input field with none.

Use: On each field.

### `render:"..."`

How an output column shows: "-" hides it; bytes, age, time, duration,
duration=ms, status or short=N. The output rule fails a value the output does
not know; the CLI owns the list.

Use: On an output field that a table must show differently.

### `telemetry:"attr"`

Records the input field on the span of the method. The field that .Key names is
recorded without it.

Use: On the field that names the item, when the method has no key, and on other
fields a trace must show.

### `template:"vars"`

Marks a string input as a Go template, whose .Vars are in the input field vars,
a map\[string]string. The API refuses a template that does not parse, that reads
a field other than .Facts, .Vars and .Hostname, or that reads a var the request
does not give. Each such method gets a generated 400 test.

Use: On an input that holds a template, such as the content of a file. Render it
with Render.

### `secret:"true"`

Redacted from the audit log, write-only with the password format in the spec
that ships, never recorded on a span.

Use: On each input that holds a password, a key or a token.

### `before:"set"`

The method's .Before step sets the field. It is not in the request, the command
or the UI: the caller does not send it.

Use: On the field that the step fills, such as password_hash.

### `mapstructure:"name"`

The config key of a settings field.

Use: On each field of the struct given to Config.

## What a template reads

### `.Vars.<name>`

A value from the vars of the request. The API refuses a template that reads a
var that the request does not give.

Use: For a value that the caller gives with each call.

### `.Hostname`

The hostname of the agent that renders the template.

Use: For a value that names the host.

### `.Facts.<key>`

A fact of the agent that renders the template. Facts are known only on each
host, so a fact that a host does not have fails on that host. The keys:
architecture, kernel_version, cpu_count, fqdn, service_mgr, package_mgr,
containerized, interfaces, primary_interface, routes, facts.

Use: For a value that differs from host to host.

## Generated, never edited

### `internal/behaviors/<name>/gen/`

The routes, handlers, commands, spec and tests of the behavior, from go generate
./internal/behaviors/all.

Use: Change the definition, then generate. A generated test that fails is fixed
in the definition or in internal/behavior/gen.

### `internal/behaviors/<name>/mocks/`

The double of the provider, from go generate
./internal/behaviors/&lt;name&gt;/mocks.

Use: Run it again after provider.go changes.

### `docs/docs/sidebar/reference/behaviors/<name>/`

The docs page of the behavior: the output of osapi behavior get and osapi
behavior method get, as markdown, from just cli-docs-generate (osapi cli docs
reference generate).

Use: Change the definition, then run just cli-docs-generate. A page that shows
the wrong thing is fixed in the definition, or in the get command that shows it.

### `docs/docs/sidebar/usage/cli/`

The CLI pages, from just cli-docs-generate. The help of a behavior command comes
from .Describe, .Explain, .Example and .Fails.

Use: Change the definition, then generate. A generated test that fails is fixed
in the definition or in internal/behavior/gen.

### `internal/controller/api/gen/, pkg/sdk/client/gen/, ui/src/sdk/gen/, docs/docs/gen/`

The joined spec, the SDK, the UI client and the API pages, from just generate.

Use: Change the definition, then generate. A generated test that fails is fixed
in the definition or in internal/behavior/gen.

## Not supported yet

### `A command or a shell from the caller`

There is no execute permission.

Use: Stop, and tell the person what is missing. Do not build around it.

### `Streaming and uploads`

A method that streams its output, or that takes a file in its request. A
behavior reads an object that osapi client file upload stored, with the object
building block.

Use: Stop, and tell the person what is missing. Do not build around it.

## gohai collectors

### `platform`

Returns os, name, version, version_extra, family, cpu_architecture, build. Build
it with platform.NewWith(h.Sources()).

Use: An example's fake host gives, on debian: Exists for /etc/SuSE-release,
/etc/arch-release, /etc/debian_version, /etc/enterprise-release,
/etc/exherbo-release, /etc/f5-release, /etc/gentoo-release, /etc/os-release,
/etc/redhat-release, /etc/slackware-version, /etc/system-release. On rhel:
